label: UNRESOLVED
rationale: The commit switches off the `plancher` (1,76 % x PSS) and `plafond` (130 % x PSS) of `indépendant . cotisations et contributions . assiette CSG-CRDS . abattement` when the établissement is in Mayotte; nothing else changes (same 460 parsed rules, métropole and Guadeloupe values identical). The engine confirms a semantic change for Mayotte only: at revenu brut 1 000 €/an (01/07/2025) the abattement goes 596 -> 260 and the cotisation base 404 -> 740 (cotisations 434 -> 455); at 300 000 €/an the abattement goes 44008 -> 78000 and the base 255992 -> 222000 (cotisations 23518 -> 20791); mid-range incomes are unaffected. The governing text in force (L136-3 III v.LEGIARTI000051284498, D136-5 v.LEGIARTI000049899286, carried into the cotisation base by L131-6 I v.LEGIARTI000048683707) states the floor and the ceiling without any territorial exception, so under a literal reading the after-state computes an abattement the text does not allow. But none of the 12 bounded articles mentions Mayotte, the article fixing the CSG's territorial scope (L136-1) and the Mayotte-specific social-security texts are outside the set, the library's whole Mayotte branch (CSG-CRDS non applicable, a distinct Mayotte PSS already used for the floor/ceiling before the commit) rests on Urssaf sources that are not in the corpus, and the commit cites no source. The available text therefore does not settle whether L136-3 III/D136-5 apply in Mayotte at all: UNRESOLVED. If they do, this is a MISMATCH (expected floor 829 / ceiling 61 230 on the L241-3 PSS, see expected_values_if_mismatch); if a Mayotte text excludes the floor/ceiling, it is a legitimate change resting on that outside source. Law snapshot S10 has the same texts and version ids as S9 for all 12 articles.
